source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The baby’s mouth is open wide over the areola, the lips are turned outward, and the chin rests against the breast.","B":"The baby’s lips are tucked inward and the chin remains away from the breast.","C":"The baby attaches mainly to the nipple tip and repeatedly clicks during sucking.","D":"The parent has persistent sharp nipple pain and the baby’s cheeks pull inward with each suck."}}
source_row.rationale: CDC breastfeeding guidance describes a good latch as a wide-open mouth taking in the areola, lips turned outward, and the chin against the breast. Option A matches those findings. Option B describes inward lips and poor positioning. Option C describes a shallow nipple-only latch and clicking, which suggest ineffective attachment. Option D describes persistent pain and inward cheek movement, findings that warrant latch reassessment.
source_row.source_detail: CDC Newborn Breastfeeding Basics — Signs of a good latch: mouth open wide over areola, lips turned out, chin resting against breast, regular swallowing.
